riddle: Some months have 30 days and some have 31. How many months of the year have 28 days?
When you have me, you're itching to share me. The moment you share me, you don't have me any more. What am I?
You have to break me before you can use me, and I often end up on a breakfast plate. What am I?
A farmer has 17 goats. All but 9 of them escape through a broken fence. How many goats does the farmer still have?
The more I dry, the wetter I get. What am I?
hint: You grab me after a bath.

riddle: You can catch me but never throw me. I bring sneezes and a runny nose, and I share my name with chilly weather. What am I?
What number comes next: 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
hint: Each step does the same thing.

riddle: What number comes next: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ?
hint: Look at the two numbers before.

riddle: I have a single eye, but I can't see a thing. Thread passes through me whenever you sew. What am I?
hint: Small, sharp and found in a sewing kit.

riddle: I have plenty of teeth, but I never bite anyone. I just keep your hair tidy. What am I?
I have a head and a tail but no body, and people flip me to settle arguments. What am I?
I run but never walk, I have a mouth but never talk, and I have a bed but never sleep. What am I?
You can break me without ever touching me. I'm made with words and kept with honour. What am I?
I'm full of holes, yet I can still hold water. What am I?
I have four fingers and a thumb, but I'm not alive and I have no bones. What am I?
I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old, and I cry drops of wax while I work. What am I?
Flick a switch and I fill the whole room, yet I take up no space at all. What am I?
hint: The opposite of a power cut.

riddle: I'm always on my way, but I never actually arrive. The moment you reach me, I've turned into today. What am I?
Builders set me into a solid wall so you can look straight through it, and at night I often hide behind curtains. What am I?
The more of me there is, the less you can see. Switch on a bulb and I vanish. What am I?
I can't talk, but shout at a mountain and I'll answer you in your own voice. What am I?
Feed me wood and I grow bigger; give me water and I die. What am I?
Smile at me and I smile straight back. Drop me and I'll probably crack. What am I?
hint: You check your hair in me.

riddle: I climb up hills and run down the other side, and cars ride on my back, yet I never move. What am I?
I have 88 keys, but I can't open a single door. What am I?
I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, rivers but no water, and you can fold me into your pocket. What am I?
I go up when the rain comes down. What am I?
Which is heavier: a kilo of feathers or a kilo of bricks?
hint: Check the units, not the material.

riddle: Add up the legs of a spider, a dog and a chicken. How many legs is that in total?
hint: Spiders have more than you think.

riddle: Add the number of days in a week to the number of hours in a day. What do you get?
hint: Two numbers you use every day.

riddle: How many sides do three triangles and three squares have altogether?
I'm the only prime number that is even. What number am I?
Halve me, then add 5, and you get 20. What number am I?
In a race, Rohit finished ahead of Sameer but behind Tina. Uma finished behind Sameer. Who came last?
hint: Line them up one by one.

riddle: How many zeros are there in one lakh when you write it in digits?
hint: One lakh is a hundred thousand.

riddle: Monday, Wednesday, Friday... which day comes next in this pattern?
January is to March as June is to which month?
Puppy is to dog as kitten is to what?
Unscramble the letters CIFAIPC to get the name of an ocean. Which ocean is it?
How many minutes are there in a quarter of an hour plus half an hour?
hint: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.

riddle: M, T, W, T, F, S... which letter comes next?
hint: Think of the days of the week.

riddle: I start with IS, end with AND, and have LA in the middle. What word am I?
What number comes next: 5, 10, 20, 40, ?
What number comes next: 90, 81, 72, 63, ?
On a normal dice, opposite faces always add up to 7. If 1 is on top, what number is on the bottom?
Which is the odd one out: 13, 17, 19, 21, 23?
Which is the odd one out: mango, banana, potato, apple, grapes?
I shave several times a day, yet my own beard stays exactly as it was. Who am I?
hint: I work on other people's faces.

riddle: It's pitch dark. You have one matchstick, and there's a candle, an oil lamp and a gas stove. What do you light first?
hint: Before anything else can be lit...

riddle: All bloops are razzies, and all razzies are lazzies. Are all bloops definitely lazzies?
Mr Shah has four daughters, and each daughter has exactly one brother. How many children does Mr Shah have?
hint: Do the daughters share the brother?

riddle: Which time of day is spelled the same forwards and backwards?
If today is Monday, what day of the week will it be 10 days from now?
I'm so fragile that simply saying my name breaks me. What am I?
I have bark but no bite, and a trunk but I'm no elephant. What am I?
I weigh less than a feather, yet even the strongest person can't hold me for ten minutes. What am I?
I'm an odd number, but take away one letter and I become even. What number am I?
I appear once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years. What am I?
The more of these you take, the more you leave behind you. What are they?
Multiply together every digit you can see on a phone keypad. What is the answer?
Spell me out in English and I have exactly as many letters as my value. What number am I?
hint: Try the small numbers one by one.

riddle: Which word is spelled incorrectly in every single dictionary?
What five-letter word gets shorter when you add two letters to it?
I start with T, end with T, and I'm full of T. What am I?
hint: Think of a drink, not a letter.

riddle: I can travel all around the world while staying stuck in one corner. What am I?
A butcher's assistant is 5 feet 10 inches tall and wears size 9 shoes. What does he weigh?
Two fathers and two sons go fishing. Each catches one fish, and they bring home exactly three fish. How many people went fishing?
I start with E, end with E, and usually contain only one letter. What am I?
Which building has the most stories, even if it has only one floor?
I have 13 hearts, but no lungs, no brain and no blood. What am I?
Where does 9 plus 5 give 2, and 10 plus 4 also give 2?
I'm a two-digit number. My digits add up to 13, and if you swap them you get a number 27 bigger than me. What number am I?
hint: Swapping makes it bigger, so the smaller digit comes first.

riddle: In a race, you overtake the runner in second place. What place are you in now?
hint: You took their spot, not first place.

riddle: A doctor gives you 3 tablets and says take one every half hour. How many minutes pass between the first tablet and the last?
hint: You take the first one straight away.

riddle: A bat and a ball cost 1100 rupees together. The bat costs 1000 rupees more than the ball. How many rupees does the ball cost?
A patch of lilies doubles in size every day and covers the whole pond on day 48. On which day did it cover half the pond?
O, T, T, F, F, S, S, E... which letter comes next?
A brick weighs 1 kg plus half a brick. How many kilograms does a whole brick weigh?
hint: Half a brick must weigh 1 kg.

riddle: A dark drawer holds only black socks and white socks. What is the fewest socks you must pull out to be sure of a matching pair?
A is B's sister. B is C's brother. C is D's father. What is A to D?
hint: A is the sister of D's father.

riddle: I'm black when you buy me, red while you use me and grey when you throw me away. What am I?
A man walks into a shop and asks for a glass of water. The shopkeeper suddenly shouts BOO at him. The man says thanks and leaves happy without drinking. What did he have?
What number comes next: 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ?
What number comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
When I was 6, my sister was half my age. Now I'm 40. How old is my sister?
An electric train speeds north while a strong wind blows south. Which way does the train's smoke go?
hint: What kind of train is it?

riddle: Which number between 50 and 100 is both a perfect square and a perfect cube?
Add up all the numbers on a clock face. What do you get?
A man drives with his headlights off, there's no moon and every streetlight is dead. A black cat crosses the road and he stops in time. How could he see it?
What can you add to a bucket to make it lighter?
A rider comes into town on Friday, stays for three days, and rides out on Friday. What is Friday?
hint: What does he ride in on?

riddle: A man stands on one bank of a river, his dog on the other. He calls, and the dog crosses with no bridge or boat and without getting wet. What state was the river in?
Before Mount Everest was measured and named, what was the tallest mountain on Earth?
What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon and three legs in the evening?
hint: Morning, noon and evening of life.

riddle: Which word doesn't belong: listen, silent, enlist, tinsel, lentil?
hint: Check the letters in each word.

riddle: What word can go in front of fly, cup, milk and scotch?
Tanvi is older than Arjun but younger than Neha. Kiran is older than Neha. Arjun is older than Pooja. Who is the second oldest?
Anil, Bina, Chetan, Dia and Esha sit in a row. Anil is at the left end, Bina sits next to him, Chetan is in the middle and Dia is at the right end. Who sits between Chetan and Dia?
Take one away from nineteen and you get twenty. Which kind of numbers makes this work?
hint: Think of old clocks and XIX.

riddle: If 6 friends eat 6 samosas in 6 minutes, how many samosas can 12 friends eat in 12 minutes at the same pace?
hint: One friend eats one samosa in 6 minutes.

riddle: I'm the only number whose English spelling has all its letters in alphabetical order. What number am I?
A clock takes 5 seconds to strike 6 o'clock. How many seconds does it take to strike 12 o'clock?
It takes 12 minutes to cut a log into 4 pieces. At the same speed, how many minutes to cut a log into 5 pieces?
hint: Count the cuts, not the pieces.

riddle: A snail is at the bottom of a 10 m well. Each day it climbs 3 m and each night it slips back 2 m. On which day does it reach the top?
hint: On the last day it doesn't slip back.

riddle: A girl has as many brothers as sisters, but each of her brothers has only half as many brothers as sisters. How many children are in the family?
What common English word has three double letters in a row?
Pointing at a photo, Arjun says: 'I have no brothers or sisters, but this man's father is my father's son.' How is the man in the photo related to Arjun?

Six-year-old Ravi lives on the 12th floor. Every morning he takes the lift all the way down. Coming home he rides it only to the 6th floor and climbs the rest, except on rainy days, when he rides all the way up. What does he carry on rainy days?
hint: Think about which lift buttons he can reach.

riddle: Take the first 3/7 of CHICKEN, 2/3 of CAT and 2/4 of GOAT. Which city do you get?
I'm a positive whole number that is exactly twice the sum of my own digits. What number am I?
People eat me. Remove my first letter and I'm a form of energy. Remove my first two and I'm what you do with food. Scramble my last three and you get a drink. What am I?
hint: Five letters; the drink is very Indian.

riddle: What five-letter word, written in capital letters, still reads the same when you turn it upside down?
hint: You do it in a pool.

riddle: My first two letters mean a male, my first three a female, my first four a great man, and all of me a great woman. What word am I?
On an island, everyone always lies or always tells the truth. Raj says 'Simran is a liar.' Simran says 'Raj and I are the same type.' Who tells the truth?
hint: Assume one is truthful and test it.

riddle: Three boxes are labelled Apples, Oranges and Mixed, and every label is wrong. You take a fruit from the Mixed box and it's an apple. What is in the box labelled Oranges?
hint: Its label is wrong, and the apple tells you more.

riddle: The day before yesterday Tara was 9. Next year she will turn 12. In which month is Tara's birthday?
hint: Today is a very special date.

riddle: I'm a word of six letters. Take away just one letter and twelve is what remains. What word am I?
What letter comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ?
hint: The gaps grow by one each time.

riddle: What is the smallest number bigger than 1 that leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6?
hint: Find a number all five divide into first.

riddle: I'm a two-digit number. My tens digit is twice my units digit, and if you subtract 36 from me my digits swap places. What number am I?
hint: Only a few numbers have a tens digit twice the units.

riddle: Eight friends meet and every one shakes hands exactly once with every other. How many handshakes take place?
A man pushes his car up to a hotel and immediately tells the owner he's bankrupt. What game is he playing?
hint: Dice, property and a little car token.

riddle: Four sisters are in a room. Meera is reading, Sana is cooking and Tanya is playing chess. What is the fourth sister, Isha, doing?
A big cube is painted red and then cut into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have red paint on exactly two faces?
Which five-letter word still sounds exactly the same after you remove its last four letters?
hint: You stand in one at the bank.
